name: spellkave_communicate
label: Spellkave Communicate
description: Attempt one authored speech act against one typed target. Use an observed participant or world target and an authored speech_act_id; the world authoritatively validates fresh state. An accepted utterance is echoed, may observe one bounded reply, and leaves later speech delivery in pushes. A prompt-bound answer (args_json.semantic_context), or an utterance on an action that carries an authored input form (a name or text field), also returns the next open prompt row as receipt.next_prompt, waited for inside the same reply window plus a short grace after the reply, so the next answer needs no manipulation_context read; next_prompt.status says whether a row opened, was already open, or timed out. An action's input.fields[].channel (from spellkave_manipulation_context) says how a field travels: "utterance" fields are read from what you say (plain text for one field, a JSON object keyed by field name for several); sending them in args_json is refused as utterance_required before dispatch.

target_id.description: Typed target reference to communicate with — use an observed participant or location reference (e.g. 'entity:42'). The world authoritatively validates the attempt; a bare numeric id is ambiguous and may be rejected or misresolved.

utterance.description: Optional words to say. On acceptance they are delivered to the world as dispatch_text, echoed in the receipt, and may open the bounded reply window.

args_json.description: Optional JSON argument blob, passed 1:1 to the world. Defaults to '{}'. For an authored session opener, participant_entity_ids is a nonempty list of up to 64 distinct runtime body ids; the session definition and grid remain authored, and older modules refuse this argument before dispatch. For an action that creates an entity, definition_ref names an allowed definition; the world checks the choice against the action's authored limits. A prompt-bound answer (a speech_act_id listed in a prompts[] row's responseActionIds in spellkave_manipulation_context, e.g. dm/dialog/choice/2) must carry that prompts[] row here as {"semantic_context": <row>}; without it the world rejects the answer with prompt_context_required.
